question: Does a larger number of distinct labels within each TimeSeries v11 tags Map increase normalized ID/tag processing CPU and full native PromQL cost, even when each input JSON row and total network bytes are exactly the same length and all cache hits/series/sample counts match?

single_variable: Number/distribution of labels in tags Map (8 vs36 incoming) while exact total JSON byte length per corresponding row and across phase is fixed by a varying-length deterministic payload tag. This intervention changes map content and TAGS storage size by design; do not attribute CPU exclusively to std::sort.
math_bound: 98432? Correct: 4096*24=98304 rows; normalized 9 vs37 labels per row => 884736 vs3637248 canonical label pairs processed over ingest, 4.11x; nominal introsort comparison upper work O(k log k) but exact std::sort implementation is not specified. Nominal TAGS cache 1048576/144=7281>4096 active IDs so expected 4096 misses,94208 hits and 4096 physical TAGS rows in every fresh phase; if cache totals differ, control invalid. This isolates net effect of label-pair count at equal raw wire bytes, not exact cpu cycles of sorting and hashing.
falsifier: If common projected-input SHA, per-row equal wire bytes, 98,304 sample points, 4096 stable distinct IDs, TAGS cache counts 94208 hits/4096 misses, full native avg by(project) nonempty correct labels/timestamps/numeric oracle, compiled SHA or 25% A/A control drift gates fail, classify INVALID_METHOD. A high/low ingest process CPU ratio <=max(5%,within-runner A/A drift) is NO_ROBUST_TAG_COUNT_CPU_EFFECT. In contrast, a >5% effect exceeding drift is replication needed, not an optimization approval.

limitations: Low-tag payload padding uses a different value-length distribution and may change TAGS compression. The test controls raw input bytes but cannot decompose C++ sort cost from parser, tag hashing, serialization and physical writes. Unlike R23, physical TAGS content and ID hashes legitimately differ across low/high modes.
